items.entity: FE mesh of the analysed (right-half) design domain
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1: 'The domain is parameterized using Nex=180 and Ney=30 FEs' followed by 'The right symmetric half section is optimized'. It does not say whether 180x30 is the full 6:1 beam or the half that is actually analysed. Appendix B reports the identical result (f0=0.0149, Mnd=1.57%) and states 90x30 for the symmetric half. App. B.1 calls a 180x60 mesh 'the MBB design domain'.
readings: Full 6:1 beam = 180x30 square elements; right half analysed with 90x30 elements (3:1), as in Appendix B
Right half itself meshed with 180x30 square elements (full beam would be 12:1, conflicting with Lx:Ly = 6:1)
Full 180x30 beam analysed without exploiting symmetry

items.entity: Boundary conditions of the half model (outer-end support and mid-span symmetry edge)
items.description: Supports are only drawn in Fig. 2a, which is not available. Sec. 4.1 says 'simply supported'. Sec. 4.1.1 refers to a 'roller support' for the 1-3-material results but to 'roller and hinge support' for the 4D-SF results (and the 3D MBB). The half-model BCs (symmetry condition on the cut, kinematic type of the outer support) are never written out.
readings: Roller at the outer bottom corner (u_y = 0 only) + symmetry u_x = 0 on all nodes of the mid-span edge (classic MBB half model)
Hinge/pin at the outer bottom corner (u_x = u_y = 0) + symmetry u_x = 0 on the mid-span edge

items.entity: Position and extent of the outer (roller) support
items.description: Only Fig. 2a shows where the beam is supported. The text does not say whether the support is the bottom corner node, a point inboard of the end, or how many nodes are constrained.
readings: Single node at the bottom-right corner of the half model
Small group of bottom-edge nodes at the right end (e.g., 2-4 element widths)

items.entity: Mid-span downward point load in the half model
items.description: Sec. 4.1 states F = 10^-3 for the beam of Fig. 2a (full beam, load at Lx/2). Sec. 4.1.1 analyses only the right symmetric half but does not say whether the node on the symmetry line receives F or F/2.
readings: F = 1e-3 applied downward at the top node on the symmetry edge of the half model
F/2 = 5e-4 applied at that node (full beam carries 1e-3)

items.entity: Volume fraction of the single material for Table 2, m = 1 (CASES I-III)
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 says 'For 1 material result, we use 1D SF with vf = 0.3' in the paragraph on the last (CASE III) column, and Table 12 lists 0.30 for the identical result. vf for CASE I and CASE II is not stated separately. The MBB captions (Fig. 7a legend, Fig. 8b) also list a single-material MBB run with vf = 0.40 that is not tied to any table.
readings: vf = 0.30 for all three cases
vf = 0.40 for CASE I/II (the second single-material MBB run of Fig. 7a/8b)

items.entity: Filtering/projection configuration of CASE I and CASE II
items.description: Sec. 4.1.1 defines CASE I only as 'No density filtering' and CASE II as 'With density filtering'. It is not said whether the beta-continuation projection of Eq. 30 is active in CASE I. It is also not said whether CASE II removes the projection entirely or keeps it at beta = 1.
readings: CASE I: no filter and no projection; CASE II: density filter (rmin = 3.6) only, projection omitted
CASE I: no density filter but projection (eta = 0.5, beta 1->32) applied directly to the raw variables
CASE II: density filter with projection frozen at beta = 1, eta = 0.5 (no continuation)

items.entity: Initial design (starting value of the 1D-SF design variable)
items.description: No initial guess is given in Sec. 4.1.1; only the parameter studies (Secs. 4.4.2-4.4.3) use xi = 0. The solid/void vertex sign for the 1D SF also conflicts: Eq. 4 has x11 = -1, x12 = 1, while Sec. 2.1.2 has x11 = 1, x12 = -1. This matters when converting a non-zero xi start into a density.
readings: xi = 0 in every element, i.e. uniform solid density 0.5
Uniform solid density equal to vf = 0.3 (xi = -0.4 or +0.4 depending on the vertex convention)

items.description: Secs. 3.3 and 4 state only that MMA is used, with at most 400 iterations. The move limit, the asymptote initialisation/adaptation and the subproblem constants (a0, a_i, c_i, d_i) are not given.
readings: Svanberg's standard mmasub defaults (asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7, a0 = 1, a_i = 0, c_i = 1e3-1e4, d_i = 0 or 1, move = 0.5 of variable range)
Same defaults but with a tighter move limit (about 0.1-0.2 of variable range)

items.description: Sec. 4 says only 'The maximum number of MMA iterations is set to 400'; no design-change or objective tolerance is given. Beta doubles every 75 iterations, so it reaches 32 only at about iteration 375.
readings: Run exactly 400 MMA iterations (beta = 32 for the last ~25)
Stop earlier once a change tolerance (e.g. max|dxi| < 0.01) is met after beta reaches 32

items.description: Secs. 3.3 and 4 say the objective and sensitivities are multiplied 'in every iteration' by nf = min(10/obj, 1x10^2)|loop=1. It is unclear whether nf is fixed from the first-iteration objective or recomputed every iteration. Either choice changes MMA's balance between objective and constraint.
readings: nf computed once at iteration 1 (= min(10/f0_1, 100), i.e. 100 whenever the initial strain energy < 0.1) and kept constant
nf recomputed every iteration from the current objective
No normalization (raw strain energy passed to MMA)

items.description: Sec. 3.3 defines f0 = 1/2 U^T K U (strain energy, i.e. half the compliance). Table 2 does not say whether the tabulated value includes the factor nf, or whether it refers to the analysed half or the full beam.
readings: Raw strain energy 1/2 U^T K U of the half model
nf-scaled strain energy (x100)
Compliance U^T K U, or full-beam value (x2 of the half-model value)

items.description: Only normalized Young's moduli are given (Sec. 4: E = 1 for the single 1D-SF material). Poisson's ratio is not stated anywhere.

items.entity: Void stiffness Emin in the modified SIMP law (Eq. 33)
items.description: Sec. 3.1 describes Emin only as 'a very small stiffness assigned to the void regions/elements'; no value is given.
readings: 1e-9 (relative to E = 1)

items.description: Sec. 4 says only that bilinear quadrilateral elements are used; plane stress vs plane strain is not stated.
readings: Plane stress
Plane strain

items.description: No thickness is given for the 2-D beam (Secs. 4.1, 4.1.1).
readings: Unit thickness t = 1
Other constant thickness

items.entity: Absolute beam dimensions / element size (length unit of rmin = 3.6)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only Lx:Ly = 6:1, and Sec. 4.1.1 gives rmin = 3.6 without units; no absolute lengths or element size are given. With square bilinear elements in 2-D, the result does not depend on absolute size if rmin is read in element widths.
readings: Unit element size: full beam Lx = 180, Ly = 30, rmin = 3.6 element widths
Lx = 6, Ly = 1 (element size 1/30), rmin = 3.6 element widths = 0.12 length units

locator: Sec. 4.1.1, the 2-D MBB beam, single-material case (Table 2, m = 1)
